Reuse the exact import+pandas-assertion command already proven correct
in nightly.yml:303 rather than writing a new assertion from scratch —
the only material change is swapping `--with "$wheel"` (local build
artifact) for `--with benchbox` (resolves from PyPI) and running from a
directory with no local `benchbox/` source tree in `sys.path`. Add the
new job to release-canary.yml since that file is already the scheduled,
develop-facing release-readiness canary and documents its own
concurrency/scheduling conventions; a fresh top-level workflow would

description:
`v0.3.0` published to PyPI on 2026-05-16 with a broken clean import
(`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'`, reverified live via
`uv run --isolated --no-project --with 'benchbox==0.3.0' -- python -c
'import benchbox'` run from outside the repo tree so it doesn't shadow
against the local source tree). It sat as PyPI-latest, uncaught, for
over a month (through at least 2026-07-03, per `pip index versions
benchbox` still showing `LATEST: 0.3.0`).

This happened despite `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` already having a
`test-package` job (lines ~261-304) that builds a wheel and asserts a
clean, pandas-free import — but that job tests a wheel built fresh from
the current `develop` tree on every nightly run, not the artifact
actually sitting on PyPI. Once `0.3.0` published broken, nightly kept
testing `develop`'s (possibly already-fixed) source and never flagged
that the *public* PyPI-latest install was broken for real users running
`pip install benchbox` during that window.

This TODO adds the missing signal — a scheduled check against the real
published PyPI artifact — and documents what to do when it fires,
because PyPI versions are immutable and a "fix forward" is the only
option once a bad version ships.

anti_patterns.dont: invent a new release-recovery procedure in the rollback runbook
anti_patterns.instead: the runbook should route to those, not duplicate them.
anti_patterns.why: make release-cut/release-finalize (Makefile:977-1057) is already the maintainer-facing mechanism and release-recovery-v0-3-1 is the worked precedent

anti_patterns.dont: run the PyPI-latest install check from inside the checked-out repo directory
anti_patterns.instead: this is the exact failure mode this investigation hit firsthand; run it from a directory (e.g. mktemp -d, or a job with no checkout step) that has no local benchbox/ package.
anti_patterns.why: Python silently shadows the installed package with the local benchbox/ source tree and the check will falsely pass even when the real PyPI artifact is broken

anti_patterns.dont: write a second, slightly different pandas-absence assertion string
anti_patterns.why: nightly.yml:303 already has the canonical version of this check and drift between two copies of 'the contract' is exactly the kind of accounting gap this whole work area is about

work_units.notes:
Extend `.github/workflows/release-canary.yml` (which already runs on
a daily `cron: "0 8 * * *"` schedule against `develop`, see
`env.RELEASE_CANARY_REF` near the top of the file) with a new job,
e.g. `pypi-latest-installability`, that:
  - does NOT check out the repo (or checks it out only to reuse the
    uv-setup steps) — the point is to install the *published*
    package, not build local source;
  - runs from a directory outside any checked-out repo tree (to
    avoid the exact same source-shadowing false-pass this
    investigation hit: running `import benchbox` from inside
    `/home/user/BenchBox` silently imports the local `benchbox/`
    source directory instead of the installed wheel, because Python
    adds the script's directory to `sys.path`);
  - runs: `uv run --isolated --no-project --with benchbox -- python
    -c "import importlib.util; import benchbox;
    assert importlib.util.find_spec('pandas') is None, 'core
    install must not pull pandas'; print(benchbox.__version__)"`
    (mirrors the exact assertion already used in
    `nightly.yml:303`, just against PyPI-latest instead of a
    freshly built wheel — reuse that assertion string rather than
    drifting a second copy of the "no pandas" contract);
  - fails loudly (non-zero exit, clear step name) if the import (or
    the pandas-absence assertion) fails, so `gh run list` /
    notifications surface it distinctly from the existing
    `credential-free-non-fast` canary job.
Do not gate this on any existing job in the file; it should run
independently so a PyPI-latest failure doesn't get masked by an
unrelated develop-canary failure or vice versa.
work_units.summary: Add a scheduled PyPI-latest installability canary

work_units.notes:
Add a new section to `docs/operations/release-guide.md` (currently
164 lines, ends with the release flow + pre-merge contract; no
existing rollback/yank/immutability guidance) titled something like
"## Recovering from a broken PyPI release". Cover:
  - PyPI versions are immutable: you cannot re-upload or delete-and-
    replace `X.Y.Z` once published (this is what `release-recovery-
    v0-3-1`'s `must_preserve` already asserts for `0.3.0`
    specifically — generalize that constraint into the permanent
    runbook here rather than leaving it stated only inside one
    recovery TODO).
  - Two response options and when to use each:
    (a) **yank** the broken version (`pip index` / PyPI UI "yank" —
        hides it from default resolution without deleting it,
        existing installs unaffected) when there's a safe prior
        version to fall back to;
    (b) **ship a `.postN` or the next patch** (this repo's actual
        precedent: `v0.3.0` -> `v0.3.1` recovery, not a `.post`
        suffix, per `release-recovery-v0-3-1`) when the fix is
        ready quickly and a monotonic forward release is cleaner
        than yanking.
  - Reference `make release-cut VERSION=X.Y.Z` / `make
    release-finalize VERSION=X.Y.Z` as the mechanism for the
    forward-fix path — this runbook section should not invent a
    separate recovery procedure, just point at the existing flow
    plus the yank decision point.
  - Cross-link `release-recovery-v0-3-1` as the applied precedent so
    future incidents have a worked example, not just abstract
    guidance.
work_units.summary: Document a rollback/.postN recovery runbook section
